blocks.text: A **case** is a form of a noun that shows what the noun is doing in the sentence. English has a trace of this: *I* see him, he sees *me*. Russian does it for every noun, adjective and pronoun, with endings — which is why its word order can move freely: **Ма́ма лю́бит па́пу** and **Па́пу лю́бит ма́ма** both mean *Mum loves Dad*.
Prepositions choose the case of the noun after them. **В** + prepositional means *in* (в школ**е**); **в** + accusative means *into* (в школ**у**). Learn each preposition with its case.

exercises.q: In *Ма́му лю́бит па́па*, who loves whom?
exercises.why: **Папа** is nominative (the subject); **маму** is accusative (the object). Dad loves Mum.

exercises.q: Which case is the dictionary form?
*I write **with a pencil*** — which case is *pencil*?
exercises.why: The tool you do something with: **instrumental** (карандаш**ом**).

exercises.q: *I gave the book **to my brother*** — which case is *brother*?
How many cases does Russian have?
